scene: Southern Mare Nubium, supplemental local midnight
method: Existing numerical sea tracer, historically textured Earth calibrated to physical direct illuminance, and official Radiance human-vision display conditioning. Nine built-in image_gen passes were inspected separately. Generated PNG bytes are preserved without programmatic image editing; the primary larger image is a fresh numerical render, not an upscaled AI file.

first_attempt.disposition: Rejected photographic treatment, preserved so it is not lost.

external_inputs.evidence: Historical NASA texture maps and one saved NASA/JPL Horizons geometry record.
external_inputs.reading_rule: Hash check all bytes before use. Texture is a photographic prior with Lambert shading and a display RGB atmospheric transfer. No spatial spectral radiance or future weather is supplied. External raw maps stay in ignored build storage.

rights_review.basis: NASA media guidelines generally permit educational/informational use including computer graphical simulations; source pages identify NASA/GSFC credits and no separate copyright restriction on these assets. Credits retained in this manifest and the illustration record, not baked into the image.

files.credit: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio; Reto Stockli (NASA/GSFC) and NASA Earth Observatory
files.reading_rule: Historical cloud-free map, surface observations June–September 2001 according to the source page. Not a March 2038 surface or climate prediction.

files.credit: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center; Reto Stoeckli (clouds)
files.reading_rule: Historical Blue Marble composite: two days of visible observations and a third day of thermal infrared imagery over the poles. Illustrative cloud prior, not weather predicted for 2038.
DE441, ITRF93 Earth, MEAN_ME lunar observer. TT date, airless directions; future Earth orientation is an extrapolation beyond the reported EOP interval.

passes.prompt: Create an unlabelled high fidelity photographic Earth component for a carefully constrained scientific landscape composite. Use the attached calculated globe as the exact geographical and orientation reference: visible western Pacific, Australia at right above centre with its current rotation, Southeast Asia toward lower right, north direction toward lower left. Keep this face, rotation, sphere diameter and centre. Earth is 98.6 percent illuminated: virtually full, with only a very narrow unlit upper-left limb. The supplied reference is a deliberately simple map projection with historical NASA cloud textures, approximate Lambert shading, and the warm atmospheric filter of a 1.2-atm lunar atmosphere. Give it a natural photographic finish: softly luminous warm ivory/golden cloud fields with delicate swirling weather structure over muted dark blue-green ocean and warm brown/green Australian land. Preserve the geographic shapes and broad cloud structures. Increase its photographic exposure enough to make it look like a bright Earth in the sky, while retaining cloud and land/ocean differentiation everywhere; detailed highlights, no featureless yellow ball, no scorched or volcanic texture. A restrained HDR treatment is intended, not a prediction of a single camera exposure. Keep the plain slate-blue background and square composition. Crisp fine detail without oversharpened grit; a barely perceptible atmospheric limb, no giant halo, no flare rays. No stars, labels, text, watermark, borders, inset panels or extra objects. This will be placed much smaller into the finished landscape in a later pass; do not add a landscape now.
passes.disposition: Historical-map Earth component; separately exposed photographic experiment.

passes.prompt:
Generate one immersive, exceptionally high fidelity photographic landscape, a TALL PORTRAIT 2:3 image, no text anywhere. This is the southern Mare Nubium sea on an atmosphere-bearing Moon at local midnight, with almost full Earth high overhead. Use reference 1 as the authoritative composition AND wave-shape plate. Reference 2 is the calculated average colour/framing plate. Reference 3 is a separately rendered detailed Earth component to composite at the SMALL calculated position, NOT its large reference scale.

Precise layout normalized to the full output: perfectly level sea horizon at y=65.09% of image height. Earth centre x=50.08%, y=10.22%; visible full disk width=3.108% of total image width, height=2.600% of total image height. These width/height differences follow a wide-angle rectilinear lens, no reframing or zoom. Earth angular diameter is only 1.804 degrees. It is 98.6% illuminated with a tiny upper-left dark limb. Preserve Australia/western Pacific face and the unusual rotation from reference 3, and visible cloud/ocean/continent patterns. The finished disk should be luminous warm cream/ivory with subdued teal and earthy patches, highlights protected by deliberate exposure blending. A tiny soft optical edge is sufficient, no Sun-like white blank disk and no broad corona.

The sky is CLEAR, smooth slate blue above, gradually muted blue-grey toward the horizon, following the calculated plate exactly in brightness and hue: approximate upper RGB 78,106,133 and near-horizon RGB 91,104,106. This is earthlit night rendered as an exposed photograph, not a daylight scene. No clouds in the lunar sky, no Milky Way, no star field, no pink sunset glow or rim illumination from the Sun. Sun is 60.5 degrees below the horizon. The very slight coast is only a narrow low sliver touching the extreme right horizon, starting around x=89% and rising less than 0.5% of image height at the right edge. It is distant low land, about 1.3 km away, faintly lit from high ahead. Keep the rest of the horizon open sea. No imposing mountains, shore foreground, buildings, boats, figures, vegetation close to camera or artificial objects.

Eye is 2 metres above water; camera bearing 22 degrees, pitched up 16 degrees, horizontal field of view 65 degrees. Water occupies the lower 34.9%. Build convincing non-repeating irregular waves following the geometry plate: significant height 0.626 m, dominant wavelength 27.33 m and period 10.28 seconds at lunar gravity, broad smooth rounded swells with finer short ripples driven by 3.59 m/s wind; wave travel toward NW, 63 degrees left of camera forward. Keep coherent fine ripple trains draped over larger smooth wave bodies, correct shrinking scale toward the horizon, subtle Fresnel brightening at grazing angles, deep grey-blue troughs, restrained reflected sky, naturally soft depth and no storm foam or white surf. It is textured liquid, never wrinkled foil, gritty gravel, or repetitive parallel sculpted ribbons. Actual Earth glitter is mostly toward the very bottom foreground because Earth is high; just a few isolated warm glints there. No bright vertical road from Earth to the horizon, no reflection of a low Sun. Match the sea's subdued grey-blue brightness from reference 1; subtle photographic contrast and rich resolved surface texture. No labels, captions, watermark, borders, collage seams, thumbnails or explanatory graphic elements. Final image is a single clean immersive photograph, with careful physical scale and a polished natural photographic finish.
passes.disposition: First Nubium composite preserved; rejected for naked-eye use.

passes.prompt:
Refine reference 1, keeping its beautiful photographic sea, precise horizon, portrait 2:3 framing, small right-hand coast, camera position, and clear smooth sky. Reference 2 is the calculated geometric and tonal target. Make these specific corrections only, as a clean high fidelity final composite:

1. Earth is too large. At the 1024 x 1536 output size its current disk is about 48 x 49 pixels centred (514,157). REPLACE it with a SMALLER disk exactly about 32 pixels wide and 40 pixels high, centred (513,157). This mild vertical elongation is the correct off-axis rectilinear-lens projection. Width is 3.108% of full image width; height is 2.60% of full image height. Keep the same 98.6%-lit phase, tiny upper-left dark edge, western-Pacific/Australia geography, unusual rotation, finely visible ivory cloud detail, subdued ocean and warm land patches. Blend the cleared border back into the surrounding sky with no rectangular patch. Keep Earth visibly luminous and textured. Do not turn it into a white light, enlarge it, move it or add a corona.

2. The water is somewhat too dark and contrasty versus the calculation. Lift the sea's broad midtone brightness gently, maintaining dark troughs and all natural wave detail: middle sea roughly RGB 50,62,68 on average, and near foreground approximately RGB 40,49,52, with brighter reflected-sky facets. Keep broad 0.6-m smooth swells and fine coherent ripples. No plastic sheen, stippling, whitecaps or foamy crests.

3. Remove about 85 percent of the warm sparkles. Retain only a few isolated tiny warm glints in the lowest 8 percent of the frame, mostly within x=30–58 percent, fading elsewhere. Earth is 53 degrees high: its primary mirror reflection is outside this upward-looking frame. No glimmering path reaching toward the horizon. All other water highlights are subdued blue-grey reflections of sky.

Keep horizon y=65.09% and the extreme-right coast no higher than 0.5% of the total image height. Preserve the quiet atmospheric slate-blue gradient. No clouds, star field, structures, text, labels, captions, borders, watermark or montage divisions. Natural exposure-blended photographic finish, maximum available image quality.
passes.disposition: Photographic refinement rejected after user size and midnight objections.

passes.prompt:
Use case: compositing.
Asset: one unlabeled, immersive, exceptionally high-fidelity naturalistic view of the modeled Open Moon sea at southern Mare Nubium, local midnight. This is a human-vision display approximation, not a long-exposure night photograph.

Image 1 is the authoritative PHYSICALLY RENDERED AND HUMAN-VISION-CONDITIONED REFERENCE. Preserve its composition, average luminances, almost neutral colours, atmospheric gradient, wave shapes, shadowing, water reflection distribution and small coast. Refine the numerical water into seamless, convincing real liquid while removing only sampling grain.
Image 2 is the exact ANGULAR EARTH SILHOUETTE MASK. White indicates the disk, black is not scenery. Never print this mask. Use it to keep the disk precisely located and sized.

Full-frame portrait 2:3, ideally 1024 by 1536 or higher native resolution. Rectilinear 65-degree horizontal field, 87.4-degree vertical field. Eye two metres above the water, looking 16 degrees upward. Horizon at 65.09% down; sea occupies the bottom 34.91%. Preserve the broad empty sky. Do not crop or reframe.

Earth's bright disk centre is 50.08% across, 10.217% down. The ACTUAL DISK, excluding its soft glare, spans only 3.108% of frame width and 2.60% of frame height: at 1024 by 1536 this is 31.8 by 39.9 pixels. Preserve the slight vertical elongation caused by off-axis rectilinear projection. Earth is 98.6% illuminated, very nearly full, a brilliant warm ivory light with a muted yellow surrounding glare exactly as in image 1. This common adaptation view clips most internal geography: do not invent sharp blue continents or moon craters. Keep the limb small and smooth; the soft light halo is larger than the solid disk, not an enlarged planet. This source is reflected sunlight from Earth, not a visible Sun.

Sky: smooth clear faintly cool charcoal grey, slightly lighter high in the frame, darkening gently toward the horizon as in image 1. Colour is greatly weakened at these light levels. Preserve the reference values: no vivid blue, dusk orange band, purple, black outer space, Milky Way, visible stars, lunar clouds, god rays or second light source. Do not brighten the sky to photographic daylight.

Sea: detailed yet dim dark graphite water with soft nearly neutral blue-grey reflection. Broad low swells about 0.6 m significant height, 27 m peak wavelength, 10.3-second period; NW-going, 63 degrees left of the gaze. Wind 3.6 m/s gives fine irregular ripples over the broader continuous wave shapes. Keep the reference's depth and grazing-angle foreshortening. Real water has curved connected surfaces, subtle overlapping ridges and dark troughs, never pebbles, scales, a repeating grid, metallic foil or oily plastic. No exaggerated steep waves, breaking crests, foam, spray or added bioluminescence. Low light reduces fine contrast, so do not artificially sharpen every ripple.

Keep the exact sparse pale-warm specular flecks visible mainly in the bottom 10% and slightly left of centre, following the calculated geometry. They should be short interrupted liquid highlights, never a continuous bright path from the horizon. The main mirror direction of high Earth lies BELOW the frame. Keep the near-horizon sea quiet and dark.

Land is only the almost invisible low sliver at the extreme right horizon, beginning about 89% across; maximum height less than 0.5% of the image height. No mountain range, foreground shore, buildings, boats, people or invented terrain.

Finishing: rich physical presence through coherent liquid geometry and restrained light, no camera noise, compositing seams or sharpening halos. Preserve the reference's darkness and limited colour. Absolutely NO text, labels, numbers, symbols, scene ID, legend, captions, watermarks, border or inset.
passes.disposition: Human-model-guided first pass; horizon and Earth placement drifted.

passes.prompt:

Correct ONLY the composition geometry of image 1 to match images 2 and 3. Keep the full 2:3 portrait image; do not crop.

Reproject the low liquid swells naturally into the remaining bottom 34.9% of the frame; preserve their fine physical texture, darkness and the foreground reflection patches. Keep the extremely low coast confined to the extreme right horizon; move it down together with the horizon.

2. Move the solid Earth disk DOWN by 30 pixels: its centre must be at x=513,y=157 in a 1024 by 1536 image, or 50.08% across and 10.217% down at any higher native size. Reduce its solid luminous core to exactly 32 pixels wide by 40 pixels high (3.108% image width by 2.60% image height), matching image 3. Keep it slightly vertically elongated by the rectilinear perspective. Scale the existing soft halo down with it. Do not add surface detail or change its warm ivory light.

Everything else remains as in image 1: the smooth nearly neutral charcoal sky, dim continuous undulating graphite sea with subtle blue-grey reflection, sparse muted warm glints mainly at the bottom left of centre, high physical fidelity and quiet midnight atmosphere. Never add a bright reflection path from the horizon. No stars, clouds, mountains, boats, shore foreground, foam, rays, other celestial bodies or objects. preservation: Selected PNGs and these sidecars are tracked at the author’s request. Raw numerical builds, external source maps and intermediate generation passes remain in ignored results/. No labels are baked into the images.
reading_rule: Calculated view conditioned for one stated display/adaptation model, not a literal validated human percept. The generator’s native-resolution and geometry limits are explicit in the review. First requested Ingenii image and prior Procellarum selection remain preserved.
